---
name: reach-wall-is-dram-plateau
description: "The reach's super-linear wall is a one-time L3-crossover DRAM step + 3-point noise, NOT growing memory hierarchy nor super-Theta(x)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 17146623-6a48-466c-b15b-22809b864a72
---

S529 mechanism measurement (`mem_hierarchy_wall.py`) of the BIG_Q kernel
`_mul61` per-element wall vs array size resolves the item-5 reach falsifier
(does streaming tame the 5.80×/Δn=2 super-linear wall, or is it super-Θ(x)?):

- `_mul61` ns/elem is bowl-shaped: ~28 ns @8 KiB (dispatch-bound), MIN **12.8 ns
  @32 KiB (L1)**, rising to a **flat ~90–110 ns plateau once >L3 (≥64 MiB, DRAM)**
  — a ~7–8× cache penalty that is a ONE-TIME STEP hit by every reach n≥18 (working
  set already >L3=32 MiB), not a per-n growing term.
- Across the reach DRAM regime (185 MiB→2.6 GiB) per-element growth is only
  ~1.08–1.11×/Δn=2 — too mild to turn the ideal Θ(x)=4× into 5.80×.
- Observed reach ratios n20→22=3.52×, n22→24=5.80×, **geo-mean 4.52×**. The two
  single-steps anti-correlate ⇒ the 5.80× S524 flagged is mostly **3-point noise**,
  consistent with Õ(x) prover (Θ(x)·polylog), NOT super-Θ(x).

Refines BOTH: S524 (5.80× ≠ evidence of super-Θ(x)) and S525 (memory hierarchy
explains the ~7× ABSOLUTE constant via the L3 crossover, but its per-Δn GROWTH is
too small to be the 5.80× source). Falsifiable prediction the detached reach tests:
n=24→26 ratio ~4.0–4.7×, n=26 wall ~5.9–7 ks. See [[reach-run-orchestration]].

explains the ~7× ABSOLUTE constant via the L3 crossover, but its per-Δn GROWTH is
too small to be the 5.80× source). Falsifiable prediction the detached reach tests:
n=24→26 ratio ~4.0–4.7×, n=26 wall ~5.9–7 ks. See [[reach-run-orchestration]].

**S535 correction (`alloc_overhead_wall.py`):** S529 measured only COMPUTE
(`_mul61` over PRE-allocated arrays). The LIVE n=26 reach, observed via /proc, is
actually **kernel/page-fault-bound, NOT compute-bound**: cumulative `stime`/(`utime`
+`stime`)=**0.695** (≈70% of CPU is the kernel handling minor page-faults), ~3.3×10⁵
faults/s, **3.1×10⁹** cumulative minor faults, majflt=0 (no swap). The unavoidable
fault floor (working set/page ≈12 GiB/4 KiB ≈3.1×10⁶) is ~1000× smaller ⇒ nearly all
faults are RE-allocations of the same Θ(x) buffers across K≈π(√x) layers. So the wall
has a THIRD leg (allocation/first-touch) that S529's bowl omits, and it can push the
WALL ratio above [4.0,5.4]× WITHOUT op-count change. Sharpened falsifier: a >5.4× wall
is consistent with Θ(x) IFF the reach is `stime`-dominated (it is) — check stime/utime,
not the wall alone. Removable headroom ≈3.3× via buffer reuse (`out=`), a constant
factor, NOT complexity (op-count Θ(x) to n=24 stands). Sample stime/utime BEFORE the
process exits — it's lost on exit.

The cycle is complete. Summary of what this cycle (S535) produced:

## What I did

The recorded NEXT ACTION — harvest the detached n=26 reach — was **not yet possible** (it's still running, ~2.85 h in, no DONE), and the constraints forbid starting a second reach. So I took **contention-safe fresh ground that directly serves the NEXT ACTION**: observing the live reach and sharpening its falsifier.

## Finding (headline)

**The live n=26 reach is page-fault/allocation-bound, not compute-bound.** Measured via `/proc` (zero contention):
- **69.5% of its CPU is kernel time** (`stime` 7012s vs `utime` 3079s)
- **3.1 billion cumulative minor page-faults**, ~3.3×10⁵/s, majflt=0 (no swap)
- The unavoidable fault floor is ~3.1×10⁶ pages → **≈1000× of faults are re-allocations** of the same Θ(x) buffers across K≈1028 layers.

This is a **third wall leg that S529's model omitted** — S529 measured steady-state `_mul61` over *pre-allocated* arrays (the compute/cache bowl) and never measured allocation/first-touch cost. A self-limiting micro-probe isolated it: reused-buffer op ~3 ns/elem (utime-dominated = S529's leg 2); fresh-allocation op ~14 ns/elem above the L2 boundary (**kernel-dominated 0.69–0.83, matching the reach's 0.695**), a ~4× penalty. The probe perturbed the reach by only +2.6% (clean falsifier point intact).

## Why it matters

It **sharpens the S529 falsifier the harvest cycle will apply**: a wall ratio >5.4× at n=26 does *not* reopen super-Θ(x) — the discriminator is `stime`/`utime`, and the reach is `stime`-dominated, so the excess is allocation overhead while op-count stays Θ(x) (confirmed to n=24). It also identifies a ~3.3× **removable** wall headroom (buffer reuse) — a constant-factor implementation win, deliberately not implemented (would break artifact reproducibility).

## Deliverables
- `alloc_overhead_wall.py` (17 selftests incl. a field-offset cross-check that caught an off-by-one /proc parse bug) + `alloc_overhead_wall_results.md` + `alloc_overhead_run.log`
- PROGRAM.md updated (S535 Done-this-era entry; reach status + sharpened falsifier in NEXT ACTION)
- Memory `reach-wall-is-dram-plateau` corrected (the wall is predominantly kernel page-faults, not compute/cache)

**Honest scope:** an in-cycle measurement refining a known wall — not a goal advance. polylog π(x) stays blocked. No BREAKTHROUGH.md (correctly).
